Rows: 183,404 units in "Power facilities"; 108,956 plants (GEM location ID) with an operating unit; operating units' Capacity (MW) summed per plant.

Ruling R22: the About sheet says records with a "TZ ID" in Other IDs (unit/phase) come partly or wholly from TransitionZero's Solar Asset Mapper (August 2025), CC BY-NC 4.0. Non-commercial data is never bundled (C6), so a plant with any such unit is left out whole: 18,723 plants with operating units, 0 of them 500 MW or more (listed under dropped).

A plant's position is its first operating unit's Latitude and Longitude; 120 kept plants have units more than 0.05 degrees apart. A plant's type is its largest Type by capacity (82 kept plants have more than one; see the types column), and its country the Country/area with the most capacity (0 span two).
Country/area names map to ISO3 through the workbook's own "Regions, area, and countries" sheet (ISO-alpha3 Code), then the app's country names.

Check: largest plants: Three Gorges Dam hydroelectric plant (CHN, hydropower) 22,500 MW; Baihetan hydroelectric plant (CHN, hydropower) 16,000 MW; Itaipu hydroelectric plant (BRA, hydropower) 14,000 MW; Xiluodu hydroelectric plant (CHN, hydropower) 13,860 MW; Belo Monte hydroelectric plant (BRA, hydropower) 11,233 MW.
